justifications.functional_suitability: Consultation Manager with SFU Media Server, Prescription Coordinator with US FHIR Adapter and EU E-Prescription Gateway, AI Inference Wrapper, and Consent & Policy Engine cover R-01 to R-04. Gaps: the AI checker is modelled as an external system and also as an internal container, and no consent management UI/API exists.
justifications.performance_efficiency: Concrete mechanisms: LiveKit SFU with adaptive bitrate, Rate Limiting & Circuit Breaker, asynchronous Pub/Sub audit dispatch, and Local Sync cache. No explicit autoscaling, caching tier, or quantified capacity targets, and synchronous audit writes in Core Telehealth Service.
justifications.compatibility: US FHIR Adapter with FHIR Mapping Engine and EU E-Prescription Gateway with National Adapter Engine (pluggable adapters, SOAP/mTLS) match R-08. Gaps: IdP integration is only generic, there are no per-country adapter specifics, and the EU/US routing is not detailed.
justifications.usability: Flutter Single-Patient / Mobile App with UI Layer and WebRTC Client serves patients and clinicians, with offline-first Local Sync. Gaps: no distinct clinician interface or portal, no consent-management UI, no pharmacy or admin channels, and no accessibility considerations.
justifications.reliability: Degraded-mode support via LiveKit adaptive bitrate, TURN/ICE Relay Service, Local Sync offline-first, circuit breaker, and Backup & Retention Manager. Gaps: no multi-zone/HA, failover, or DR design, no audio-only fallback, and a single Core Telehealth Service.
justifications.security: Strong: mTLS and JWT filter at API Gateway, SQLCipher, CMEK via Cloud KMS, TLS 1.3, Consent & Policy Engine, signed Audit & Traceability Logger, immutable Audit & Compliance Ledger. Gaps: the app calls the Payment Gateway directly, and the placement of mTLS for mobile clients and key management is unclear.
justifications.maintainability: Modular containers and components with clear responsibilities, and pluggable National Adapter Engine. Weaknesses: polyglot stack (Go, Python, Node, Java), duplicated audit and consent components across containers, and inconsistent naming and relationships such as the SQLCipher link.
justifications.portability: GKE/LiveKit, Cloud SQL, and GCS are tied to GCP, though containerized services and Flyway migrations help somewhat. The regions europe-west3 and us-central1 are addressed, but there is no IaC, abstraction layer, or multi-cloud strategy.

sensitivity_points: No autoscaling or regional SFU deployment described
Single Core Service on the join path
tradeoffs: Recording egress load competes with forwarding capacity
PERF-01.justification: LiveKit SFU is suitable, but nothing describes autoscaling, EU-region deployment or capacity for 5,000 sessions. Join validation relies on Core Service and the DB. The 10 s target is plausible but unaddressed.

sensitivity_points: Synchronous consent and audit checks on request path
tradeoffs: Audit and consent logging adds latency versus traceability
PERF-02.justification: The AI path is layered (gateway, orchestrator, wrapper, LangChain client) with no scaling, caching or latency budget. The model is external and unspecified. About 14 requests/s is modest but 3 s p95 is unsupported. Async audit helps slightly.

sensitivity_points: Adaptive bitrate and audio fallback thresholds
tradeoffs: Lower video quality versus continuity of consultation
AVAIL-01.justification: LiveKit adaptive bitrate, TURN relay and offline-first encrypted local sync address degraded links and note preservation. However, no explicit audio-only fallback below 300 kbit/s or note-sync conflict mechanism is specified.

sensitivity_points: No in-US multi-zone or DR standby described
AVAIL-02.justification: Residency is preserved by regional DBs, but no US HA, multi-zone failover, replicas or recovery runbook is defined. Backups with object locks exist, yet restoring within 1 hour is unsupported. Cross-region failover is excluded by design.

sensitivity_points: Prescription Coordinator routing may need change per country
tradeoffs: Generic adapter abstraction versus country-specific features
MOD-01.justification: National Adapter Engine hosts pluggable protocol adapters on Spring Integration, so a new country is mostly one adapter. Routing by country in the Core Service and gateway may need small changes.

sensitivity_points: No model registry or version pinning described
Version recorded per request not explicit
tradeoffs: Fast model rollout versus validation under MDR traceability
MOD-02.justification: Model Client Adapter isolates the model and audit loggers with an immutable ledger support traceability. But no model registry, versioned deployment, canary or rollback mechanism is described, and logging inputs and version is only implied.

sensitivity_points: Consent engine in Core Service uses single shared instance
tradeoffs: Strict residency versus clinicians' cross-border care
SEC-01.justification: Consent & Policy Engine intercepts access and audit logging exists, but a US-patient request by an EU clinician has no explicit cross-region data path or denial flow. Client-side consent enforcement is weak. Server enforcement is only partly described.

sensitivity_points: No revocation propagation to downstream consumers
Client-cached consent flags may be stale
tradeoffs: Offline consent caching versus timely revocation
SEC-02.justification: Consent states are stored in the ledger and engines check purposes, but there is no withdrawal workflow, propagation to research sharing, or 24 h verification. No research-sharing component exists. Offline client caching risks stale consent.
